name: Carol Cashell
highlight: The Cork swimmer took the first turn on a two-way Channel relay in 2013 and completed the Triple Crown of Marathon Swimming in 2017.
biography: Carol Cashell of Cork first appears here as the opening swimmer for Crosóige Mara. On 13 July 2013 she stepped ashore at Abbot’s Cliff before starting the six-person relay to France and back. Four years later she crossed solo in 10 hours 18 minutes with Andy and James King on Louise Jane.

Cashell’s 2013 Manhattan swim and her 2017 Catalina and English Channel solos form the Triple Crown of Marathon Swimming. She also raced for Sandycove Island Swim Club in the pool, winning the women’s 35–39 short-course 400 metres freestyle at Mallow in December 2017. She entered the Ireland Marathon Swimming Hall of Fame in 2021.

lines.label: Team result
lines.text: The six swimmers completed the first leg in 10:18:59 and the return in 10:10:01. Their combined time was 20:29:00.

lines.label: Route and clocks
lines.text: Cashell began the first hour at 01:14 at Abbot’s Cliff. The team landed south of Cap Gris-Nez, then returned to Shakespeare Beach. The start and duration imply a finish around 21:43.

questions.label: How long did Carol Cashell’s solo English Channel swim take?
questions.value: She swam from England to France in 10 hours 18 minutes on 26 August 2017.

questions.label: Who swam first for Crosóige Mara?
questions.value: Carol Cashell swam the first turn in the six-person, two-way relay in 2013.

questions.label: Which swims completed Carol Cashell’s Triple Crown?
questions.value: Manhattan in June 2013, Catalina in July 2017 and the English Channel in August 2017.
